key_insight: ACE-Data-0 proposes a human-centric ambient capture engine that records embodied behavior in real homes, aiming to observe the full perception-action loop as people move, manipulate objects, and interact with the environment over time. The core breakthrough is turning everyday living spaces into a multimodal data engine for embodied intelligence.
problem_solved: Embodied AI lacks integrated data that jointly captures first-person perception, body motion, hand-object interaction, object state changes, audio, and touch across time. Existing datasets usually split these signals across different views, modalities, or scales, making it hard to study real-world goal-directed behavior end-to-end.
method: Uses an Ambient Capture Engine (ACE) to collect human-centric, in-home embodied interactions in natural settings.
Synchronizes multiple modalities, including first-person vision, whole-body motion, dexterous manipulation, object state, sound, and touch.
Frames data collection around goal-driven human activity to preserve the temporal evolution of perception and action.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this kind of dataset can improve training and evaluation of embodied agents that need to understand and act in the real world, not just in isolated lab settings. It supports richer benchmarks for perception, manipulation, and multimodal reasoning in home environments.

paper_title: ACE-Data-0: Human-Centric Ambient Capture as Embodied Data Engine
paper_authors: Yukang Cao, Haozhe Xie, Beichen Wen, Runmao Yao, Yinghao Liu
